meta.name: Implement GET /links with optional tag filter

from-feature.criterion: The system shall return 200 and a JSON array from GET /links, empty when no links are stored.
The system shall order listed links most recently created first.
The system shall include every stored link in the listing, reporting a null title rather than omitting an untitled link.
If the stored links cannot be read, then the system shall return 500 and shall not return an empty array, so that a failure to read is never reported as an empty shelf.
When links are listed with a tag filter, the system shall return exactly the links carrying that tag.

context.data-model:
From list-links: Reads Link(id, url, title, created_at) -- owned by save-link. This feature owns no entity of its own and adds no column; the ordering it guarantees is over created_at.
From tag-links: Tag(id integer pk, name text unique not null) LinkTag(link_id fk Link.id, tag_id fk Tag.id, primary key both)
context.prd-excerpt:
Feature "List saved links" (list-links, must-have): A GET endpoint returning every saved link as a JSON array, newest first by created_at. No pagination: the fixture's scale does not justify it, and adding it would introduce a second dimension of behaviour to verify.
User story: As someone collecting links, I want to see what I have saved, newest first, so that I can find the thing I saved this morning without scrolling.
Considerations (list-links): Ordering is part of the contract, not an incidental detail, so it carries its own acceptance criterion. A test that only checks the count would pass against an implementation that returns rows in insertion order and silently breaks later.
Feature "Tag links" (tag-links, should-have), the filter half only: Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag. Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column.
Considerations (tag-links): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct. This is an implementation constraint carried from the feature's notes/considerations block; it is NOT an acceptance criterion and has no id.
Endpoint scope: GET /links and its tag filter are ONE endpoint and ONE task. Two feature passes independently produced a listing endpoint (list-links named "GET /links" verbatim; tag-links required a filter on "the list endpoint"). They were merged so that two tasks do not write the same route handler. Do not add a second listing route.
No /api prefix. The PRD never mentions one. The path is exactly /links. No pagination. Do not add limit, offset, page or cursor parameters.

task.objective: Add a GET /links handler to app/api/links.py that returns every stored link as a JSON array ordered most recently created first, accepts an optional tag query parameter that filters to exactly the links carrying that tag, and returns 500 rather than an empty array when the stored links cannot be read.

requirements.requirement: Modify `app/api/links.py`. Do not create a new module and do not modify `app/main.py`. Add the handler to the existing `router` object; leave the existing POST /links handler unchanged.

Add these imports to `app/api/links.py`, keeping the ones already present:
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Query from sqlalchemy import select from sqlalchemy.exc import SQLAlchemyError from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.db import get_db from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag from app.schemas.link import LinkRead

Build the query as follows:
stmt = select(Link) if tag is not None: stmt = ( stmt.join(LinkTag, LinkTag.link_id == Link.id) .join(Tag, Tag.id == LinkTag.tag_id) .where(Tag.name == tag) ) stmt = stmt.order_by(Link.created_at.desc(), Link.id.desc())
The secondary sort on `Link.id.desc()` is required, not optional: two links created inside the same test can share a created_at value, and without the tiebreaker the ordering guaranteed by list-links criterion 2 is not deterministic.
`Tag.name == tag` is an exact, case-sensitive comparison. Do not apply `lower()`, `ilike`, `collate("NOCASE")` or any other case folding. Carried from the tag-links notes/considerations block ("Tag names are matched case-sensitively") as an implementation constraint, not as an acceptance criterion.
When no links are stored, the handler returns an empty list and FastAPI serialises it as `[]` with status 200. Do not special-case the empty result and do not return 404 for it.
Add no pagination parameters (`limit`, `offset`, `page`, `cursor`, `per_page`) and no second listing route. The tag filter is the only query parameter this endpoint accepts.

test-requirements.test:
Create test file: `tests/test_list_links.py`
Module imports:
import pytest from datetime import datetime from sqlalchemy.exc import SQLAlchemyError from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from app.main import app from app.db import get_db from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag
Every test below takes the `client` and `db_session` fixtures from tests/conftest.py, except test 5, which builds its own TestClient.

Test: test_get_links_always_returns_200_and_a_json_array Pattern is `ubiquitous`, so assert the invariant holds after every operation, not once. - GET /links on the empty database. Assert response.status_code == 200. - Assert isinstance(response.json(), list) and response.json() == [] - Add one Link via db_session: db_session.add(Link(url="https://example.com/a", title="A", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0))) db_session.commit() - GET /links again. Assert status_code == 200, isinstance(json, list), len(json) == 1 - Add a second Link via db_session: db_session.add(Link(url="https://example.com/b", title=None, created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 2, 12, 0, 0))) db_session.commit() - GET /links again. Assert status_code == 200, isinstance(json, list), len(json) == 2

Test: test_links_are_ordered_most_recently_created_first Pattern is `ubiquitous`, so assert the ordering still holds after a further insert. - Insert three links via db_session with explicit, distinct created_at values: oldest = Link(url="https://example.com/1", title="one", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)) middle = Link(url="https://example.com/2", title="two", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 2, 9, 0, 0)) newest = Link(url="https://example.com/3", title="three", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 3, 9, 0, 0)) db_session.add_all([oldest, middle, newest]) db_session.commit() They are added in the order oldest, middle, newest so that insertion order differs from the expected output order and an implementation returning rows in insertion order fails. - GET /links. Assert [item["url"] for item in response.json()] == ["https://example.com/3", "https://example.com/2", "https://example.com/1"] - Insert a fourth link: db_session.add(Link(url="https://example.com/4", title="four", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 4, 9, 0, 0))) db_session.commit() - GET /links again. Assert [item["url"] for item in response.json()] == ["https://example.com/4", "https://example.com/3", "https://example.com/2", "https://example.com/1"]

Test: test_untitled_links_are_listed_with_a_null_title Pattern is `ubiquitous`, so assert the property over every element of the listing. - Insert via db_session: db_session.add_all([ Link(url="https://example.com/titled", title="Has a title", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0)), Link(url="https://example.com/untitled", title=None, created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 2, 10, 0, 0)), ]) db_session.commit() - GET /links. Assert len(response.json()) == 2, so the untitled link is not omitted. - Assert all("title" in item for item in response.json()), so the key is present on every element. - Find the element whose url == "https://example.com/untitled"; assert its "title" is None. - Find the element whose url == "https://example.com/titled"; assert its "title" == "Has a title".

Test: test_tag_filter_returns_exactly_the_links_carrying_that_tag Pattern is `event-driven`: one action, a GET with a tag filter, produces one observable outcome, exactly the tagged links. Build the tag rows directly through db_session, because POST /links/{link_id}/tags is task L3-006 and does not exist yet. - Insert three links via db_session: link_a = Link(url="https://example.com/a", title="A", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 8, 0, 0)) link_b = Link(url="https://example.com/b", title="B", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 2, 8, 0, 0)) link_c = Link(url="https://example.com/c", title="C", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 3, 8, 0, 0)) db_session.add_all([link_a, link_b, link_c]) db_session.commit() # so the links have ids - Insert the tags via db_session: tag_python = Tag(name="python") tag_other = Tag(name="Python") # a different tag: names are case-sensitive db_session.add_all([tag_python, tag_other]) db_session.commit() # so the tags have ids - Insert the join rows via db_session: db_session.add_all([ LinkTag(link_id=link_a.id, tag_id=tag_python.id), LinkTag(link_id=link_c.id, tag_id=tag_python.id), LinkTag(link_id=link_b.id, tag_id=tag_other.id), ]) db_session.commit() - GET /links?tag=python Assert status_code == 200 Assert [item["url"] for item in response.json()] == ["https://example.com/c", "https://example.com/a"] which is exactly the two carrying "python", still newest first, with link_b excluded. - Additional assertion for the case-sensitivity constraint carried from the tag-links notes/considerations block, not for the criterion: GET /links?tag=Python . Assert [item["url"] for item in response.json()] == ["https://example.com/b"], proving "python" and "Python" are not folded together. - GET /links?tag=nonexistent . Assert status_code == 200 and response.json() == [] - GET /links with no tag parameter. Assert len(response.json()) == 3, proving the filter is genuinely optional.

exports.interface:
GET /links GET /links?tag={tag}
Query parameters: tag: str, optional. Exact, case-sensitive match against Tag.name. When absent, every stored link is returned.
Response 200: application/json, a JSON array of LinkRead objects, ordered by created_at descending then id descending. Empty array when nothing matches.
[ { "id": 3, "url": "https://example.com/3", "title": "three", "created_at": "2026-01-03T09:00:00" } ]
"title" is null rather than omitted when the link has no title.
Response 500: application/json, {"detail": "Failed to read stored links"} Returned when the stored links cannot be read. Never an empty array.
No pagination parameters. No /api prefix.
